stories.headline: Anthropic Reaches $1 Trillion Valuation on Secondary Markets, Surpassing OpenAI's $880B

key_facts.fact: On Forge Global, a private share marketplace, Anthropic's implied valuation has climbed to roughly $1 trillion, surpassing OpenAI which trades at $880 billion on the same platform.
Anthropic's last primary funding round, led by GIC and Coatue roughly three months ago, valued the company at $380 billion — less than half of what the secondary market now implies.
Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate surged from $9 billion late last year to $30 billion by March 2026, driven largely by breakout adoption of Claude Code among developers.
A shortage of available shares is fueling buyer frenzy. One shareholder offered to sell at a $1.15 trillion valuation, while a 'very well known growth fund' bid at $1.05 trillion.
Anthropic has reportedly been rejecting investment offers at an $800 billion valuation in recent days, while current shareholders report being inundated with unsolicited approaches.
OpenAI's position on secondary markets looks markedly different: interest has been thin, with buyers unwilling to match the price from the company's last fundraise.

stories.headline: ASML Plans to Build at Least 60 EUV Machines in 2026, Up 36% From 2025 Sales

key_facts.fact: ASML plans to make at least 60 of its standard EUV lithography machines in 2026, a 36% increase over the number it sold in 2025, as it races to meet demand for AI chip production.
ASML is the sole supplier of EUV lithography machines needed to manufacture cutting-edge AI chips at scale, giving it a monopoly position in the supply chain.
ASML's order backlog stood at €38.8 billion at the end of 2025, and the company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to €34–39 billion, well above prior analyst estimates.
The production ramp at ASML's Veldhoven headquarters in the Netherlands highlights the critical bottleneck in AI chip manufacturing infrastructure.

stories.headline: ASML Targets 60 EUV Machines in 2026, Pledges No Bottleneck for AI Chip Boom

key_facts.fact: ASML CFO Roger Dassen said the company targets shipping 60 units from its current-gen EUV portfolio in 2026, with room to ramp up to 80 units in 2027 — compared to 44 sold in 2025
ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet pledged the company would prevent supply bottlenecks 'by all possible means' at the AGM, with both logic and memory demand continuing to outpace supply
ASML raised its 2026 revenue outlook to €36 billion-€40 billion after Q1 results showed €8.8 billion in sales and €2.8 billion in net income

Memory makers have sold out inventory for the year and expect supply constraints to persist past 2026, with 51% of Q1 EUV orders coming from memory customers (SK Hynix alone grabbing 20 machines for HBM4 production)
TSMC is holding off on ASML's $400M high-NA EUV platform, with Kevin Zhang telling Reuters the chipmaker continues to leverage existing EUV technology for smaller and faster chips

stories.headline: Beijing Auto Show 2026 Opens as World's Largest, With Humanoid Robots at Every Booth

key_facts.fact: Auto China 2026 features 1,451 vehicles including 181 world premieres and 71 concept cars across a record-breaking 380,000 square meters of exhibition space at two venues

Humanoid robots and robot dogs were at seemingly every other booth; XPeng plans mass production of its IRON humanoid robot in late 2026, while many other companies simply bought Unitree robots as booth attractions
Geely unveiled China's first native robotaxi prototype, a purpose-built driverless model with over 3,000 TOPS of computing power, alongside a concept featuring a humanoid robot standing guard
The show is now the largest auto show in the world, with 17 halls each containing more EV models than are available in the entire US market
Even non-auto companies like Dreame (robot vacuum maker) displayed electric sports car concepts, while Huawei's Maextro luxury sedan targets the Rolls-Royce segment

stories.headline: China Launches Pakistan's PRSC-EO3 Earth Observation Satellite, Deepening Space Cooperation

key_facts.fact: China successfully launched Pakistan's PRSC-EO3 earth observation satellite into planned orbit on April 26, along with internet test and environment monitoring satellites
Pakistan described the launch as a major milestone in the country's Earth observation capability, with the indigenous EO3 satellite entering its planned orbit
The satellite was launched on a Chinese Long March rocket, marking another step in China-Pakistan space cooperation
The launch comes amid Pakistan's role as host for US-Iran peace negotiations, highlighting the country's deepening ties with both China and the West

stories.headline: DOJ Drops Criminal Probe of Fed Chair Powell, Clearing Path for Trump's Nominee Warsh

key_facts.fact: The Justice Department ended its criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, removing a major political obstacle
The decision clears the path for Kevin Warsh, Trump's nominee to replace Powell as Fed chair, whose Senate confirmation had been stalled
Sen. Thom Tillis, who had blocked Warsh's confirmation over the probe, said he is now ready to move ahead with the process
The probe was widely viewed as political pressure on Fed independence; DOJ also dropped an investigation into Fed building renovations

stories.headline: SpaceX, Anduril Among 12 Firms to Win $3.2B Golden Dome Space Interceptor Contracts

key_facts.fact: The US Space Force awarded approximately $3.2 billion in contracts across 12 companies for the Golden Dome missile defense program's early phase
Selected companies include SpaceX, Anduril, Palantir, Aalyria Technologies, Scale AI, Swoop Technologies, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, and RTX (Raytheon)
The program focuses on building a space-based satellite network to detect and track missile threats including hypersonic weapons, using hundreds of LEO satellites instead of traditional ground radar
SpaceX will contribute satellite constellation expertise and high-speed inter-satellite laser communication links for rapid data relay
Anduril is expected to develop AI-powered command-and-control systems to process real-time satellite data, identify threats, and coordinate automated defense responses

stories.headline: Epoch AI: Google Controls ~25% of Global AI Compute, Mostly via Custom TPUs

key_facts.fact: Google holds about one quarter of global cumulative AI compute capacity as of Q4 2025, making it the largest single owner of AI compute
About three quarters of Google's compute comes from its in-house designed TPU chips rather than Nvidia GPUs, unlike other hyperscalers who rely predominantly on Nvidia
Five hyperscalers (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) collectively hold an estimated 71% of global AI compute as of Q4 2025, up from 63% in Q1 2024
Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian says AI chip and model demand and revenue justify Google's massive compute spending
Many AI labs including OpenAI and Anthropic depend almost entirely on hyperscalers for access to their R&D and inference compute

stories.headline: Epoch AI: Google Controls ~25% of Global AI Compute With 3.8M TPUs, Leading All Hyperscalers

key_facts.fact: Google is the largest single owner of AI compute, holding about one quarter of global cumulative capacity as of Q4 2025, according to Epoch AI's Chip Ownership data.
Google's compute comes primarily from its own custom TPU chips rather than Nvidia's GPUs, making it unique among hyperscalers. Google has approximately 3.8 million TPUs and 1.3 million GPUs.
Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle — collectively hold an estimated 71% of the world's cumulative AI compute, up from 63% in Q1 2024.

Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian told the Financial Times that demand and revenue justify the massive compute investment, arguing the company's AI chips and models can help the data centre business gain ground.

stories.headline: Intellia to Report First-Ever Phase 3 In Vivo CRISPR Gene-Editing Data on Monday

key_facts.fact: Intellia Therapeutics announced it will report topline data from HAELO, the first-ever Phase 3 trial of an in vivo CRISPR gene-editing therapy, at 8:00 AM EDT on April 27
Intellia shares jumped 19.3% after hours to $16.26 on April 25, following a 14.1% decline during regular trading to $13.63
HAELO is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with 80 participants evaluating a single 50mg infusion of lonvoguran ziclumeran for hereditary angioedema (HAE)
In Phase 1/2 data, 31 out of 32 patients on the 50mg dose stayed attack-free without ongoing prophylaxis, with follow-up reaching three years
If Phase 3 data are positive, Intellia plans a US biologics license application in H2 2026, with potential launch in H1 2027; the company holds $605.1 million in cash
The therapy targets the KLKB1 gene in the liver to knock down kallikrein, a key protein in the swelling cascade; rivals include Ionis's Dawnzera and KalVista's Ekterly

stories.headline: Musk Drops Fraud Claims Against OpenAI, Narrowing $134B Trial to Two Key Claims

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers dismissed Musk's fraud and constructive fraud claims at his own request on April 24, leaving only two of the original 26 claims: unjust enrichment and breach of charitable trust.
Jury selection is scheduled for Monday April 27 at federal court in Oakland, California, with opening arguments to follow on Tuesday.
Musk is seeking up to $134 billion in damages from OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming OpenAI betrayed its founding nonprofit mission. He said proceeds would go to OpenAI's charitable arm if he wins.

Musk alleges OpenAI deviated from its founding nonprofit mission after securing billions from Microsoft and transitioning to a for-profit structure. He contributed $38 million in seed funding in 2015.
Musk strategically dropped fraud claims to focus jurors on whether OpenAI benefits humanity rather than serving as a 'wealth machine,' avoiding complex evidentiary hurdles around intent.
OpenAI, Altman, Brockman, and Microsoft have denied the allegations, calling the lawsuit 'part of Musk's ongoing pattern of harassment' and accusing him of trying to benefit his own AI company, xAI.

stories.headline: Russia's Economy Minister Admits Reserves Depleted as Central Bank Cuts Rate and Lawmaker Warns of Revolution

key_facts.fact: Economy Minister Maxim Reshetnikov told a business conference that economic reserves 'have largely been used up' and the macroeconomic situation is 'substantially more difficult'

Russia's central bank cut the benchmark interest rate to 14.5% on April 25, the fifth consecutive half-point reduction, with Governor Nabiullina citing the Middle East conflict as a significant external risk
Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov warned parliament that 'a repeat of what happened in 1917 awaits us' by autumn if urgent financial and economic measures are not adopted
Putin revealed in an April 15 televised meeting that GDP shrank by a combined 1.8% in January and February, with manufacturing, industrial production, and construction all negative
Sweden's military intelligence chief said Russia's economy is weaker than it appears and its military-industrial complex is losing money, ravaged by corruption, and dependent on state bank lending

stories.headline: Samsung Mobile Division Faces First-Ever Annual Loss as AI Devours Memory Supply

key_facts.fact: Samsung MX head TM Roh warned company leadership the mobile division could post its first-ever net loss on smartphones in 2026, despite strong Galaxy S26 sales
Nvidia's upcoming Vera AI CPU will use up to 1.5 TB of LPDDR5x memory; a single server rack with 36 Vera CPUs consumes enough RAM for 4,600 Galaxy S26 Ultra devices
RAM now accounts for more than a third of the cost of building a budget phone in mid-2026, roughly doubling the cost of memory and storage according to Counterpoint Research
Samsung Semiconductor smashed records in Q1 2026, earning an estimated $38 billion (KRW 57.2 trillion) in profit — more than seven times its Q1 2025 net
DRAM production in 2027 could fall 40% short of expected demand even with best-case improvements in output, according to Nikkei Asia
Motorola raised prices on its Moto G budget phones by up to 50%; Samsung added $50-$100 price hikes to Galaxy A37, A57, Z Flip 7, Z Fold 7, and Tab S11

stories.headline: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab Grows to ~140 Staff, Hiring Most From Meta

key_facts.fact: LinkedIn profile analysis shows Thinking Machines Lab has hired more researchers from Meta than from any other employer, with headcount now at approximately 140.
Thinking Machines Lab was founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati and raised a record $2 billion seed round at a $12 billion valuation.

The hiring pattern is notable given Meta's own aggressive AI push, including a 'superintelligence' lab, multibillion-dollar AI infrastructure deals, and reported offers of up to $1 billion to recruit individual AI researchers.

stories.headline: Trump Cancels Witkoff and Kushner's Trip to Pakistan for Iran Peace Talks

key_facts.fact: Trump canceled the planned trip of envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Pakistan for direct talks with Iran, saying 'We have all the cards'
Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi headed to Islamabad separately for 'key consultative meetings' with Pakistani officials despite the US pullback
Iran shared a 'workable framework' with Pakistan on ending the war, even as the US held back its envoy for talks
The cancellation reverses course from earlier in the week when the White House announced Witkoff and Kushner would travel to Pakistan for direct talks with Iran
Iran's FM was also expected to travel to Russia following Islamabad consultations, broadening the diplomatic landscape

stories.headline: US Has Depleted Half Its Most Expensive Missiles in Iran War, Raising Taiwan Deterrence Concerns

key_facts.fact: The US military may have already used up half of its most expensive missiles in the Iran war, with stockpile rebuilding estimated to take up to 4 years
The depletion of stealth missile stockpiles raises concerns about US ability to deter China over Taiwan
Critical missile stockpiles have been drained as a yearslong rebuild now looms, according to defense analysts and reporting from multiple outlets
The stockpile depletion comes as the US simultaneously expands spending on the Golden Dome missile defense program and boosts F-35 fleet after a record defense budget

stories.headline: Wisconsin Regulators Force Data Centers to Pay Full Energy Costs, Block Cost-Shifting to Residents

key_facts.fact: Wisconsin's Public Service Commission unanimously approved a modified special energy rate requiring data centers to pay 100% of new natural gas plant costs, rejecting We Energies' plan that would have shifted 25% to residential customers
The decision affects Microsoft's Mount Pleasant campus (~900 MW) and a $15 billion Port Washington project for OpenAI and Oracle that could use up to 3.5 GW at full build-out
We Energies plans to spend $19.3 billion on new electricity generation over five years, aiming to double its energy generating capacity by 2030 to serve data centers
Regulators lowered the mandatory rate threshold from 500 MW to 100 MW and extended service agreements from 10 to 15 years to prevent cost-shifting during construction phases
Nearly 70% of Wisconsin voters said data center costs outweigh their benefits; more than 2,000 public comments were submitted opposing the original plan
We Energies said the new rate structure could serve as a model for other states looking to meet data center needs while protecting other energy customers
